subsystems.name: Tissue sectioning and preservation
subsystems.role: turns a real tissue into a thin, flat slice whose molecules stay where they were.

subsystems.name: Spatially barcoded capture surface
subsystems.role: a slide or array on which every position carries a known DNA barcode.
parts: oligo-dT capture probes with spatial barcodes
array spots, beads, or patterned barcode patches

subsystems.name: Molecular capture and conversion
subsystems.role: mRNA is released from the cell, caught by the nearest barcode and copied into cDNA.

subsystems.name: Library preparation and readout
subsystems.role: converts captured molecules into data — by sequencing or by imaging.

subsystems.name: Imaging and registration
subsystems.role: pairs tissue morphology with the barcode grid.

subsystems.name: Computational pipeline
subsystems.role: turns barcodes and pixels into a cell-type map.

buildSteps.title: Design the barcodes
buildSteps.detail: A whitelist of spatial barcodes is generated and printed or synthesised onto the capture surface, each position randomised so neighbouring spots never share a code.

buildSteps.title: Section the tissue
buildSteps.detail: The sample is snap-frozen or fixed, then cut into sections a few micrometres thick and mounted on the barcoded slide.

buildSteps.title: Image the section
buildSteps.detail: A stained microscope image is taken first, giving the morphology and the fiducial positions needed later to align pixels with barcodes.

buildSteps.title: Permeabilise and capture
buildSteps.detail: The membrane is gently opened so mRNA diffuses a short distance and hybridises to the capture oligos directly beneath it.

buildSteps.title: Reverse-transcribe and collect
buildSteps.detail: The captured mRNA is copied into cDNA carrying its spatial barcode, then lifted off the slide into a tube as one pooled library.

buildSteps.title: Sequence
buildSteps.detail: The library is sequenced; each read begins with a barcode that says which position on the slide it came from.

buildSteps.title: Alternative readout: image in place
buildSteps.detail: Imaging-based platforms skip sequencing-by-synthesis and instead hybridise fluorescent probes in repeated cycles, reading out hundreds to thousands of genes while the tissue stays intact.

buildSteps.title: Align and quantify
buildSteps.detail: Reads or pixel intensities are mapped back onto the tissue image, and the barcode grid is registered to the histology.

buildSteps.title: Analyse
buildSteps.detail: Counts are normalised, spots are deconvolved into cell types or cells are segmented, and spatial patterns — domains, gradients, cell-cell contacts — are called.

prerequisites.why: provides the cheap, massively parallel readout that makes whole-transcriptome spatial capture affordable.
the idea of tagging every molecule with a cell- or position-specific code is inherited directly from droplet single-cell RNA-seq.

prerequisites.tech: High-resolution fluorescence microscopy and probe chemistry
prerequisites.why: imaging-based spatial methods depend on resolving and erasing many rounds of fluorescent signal in intact tissue.
reads must be mapped to a known genome before they can be counted.
most capture-array spots hold several cells, so assigning signal to individual cells is still an inference.
capture efficiency varies strongly by tissue type, and fixing chemistry that preserves both morphology and RNA is finicky.

pathway.milestone: commercial platforms in routine research use — array capture such as 10x Visium with spots around 55 µm wide spaced about 100 µm apart for whole transcriptomes, and imaging panels such as MERFISH, Xenium, CosMx and MERSCOPE for targeted gene sets at subcellular resolution
pathway.unlocks: tumour microenvironments, brain atlases and developmental maps drawn at cell-type level.

pathway.milestone: whole-transcriptome profiling at true single-cell resolution across a full tissue section, with reliable segmentation
pathway.unlocks: removes the trade-off between gene breadth and spatial precision.

pathway.milestone: routine multimodal spatial assays combining RNA with protein and chromatin marks on the same section
pathway.unlocks: links cell identity, state and regulatory programme in place.

pathway.milestone: three-dimensional reconstruction of whole organs and validated clinical use in pathology
pathway.unlocks: spatial diagnostics and a genuine physical atlas of human tissue.
